title: What is Agentify ERP? A plain-English guide for property firms
description: What Agentify ERP is, who it is for, what the Real Estate and Construction products cover, and how to try it free before you decide.
faq: What is Agentify ERP?
Agentify ERP is a cloud CRM and ERP for real estate agencies and construction companies. It runs in the browser and has an Android app.
Who is Agentify ERP for?
Property dealers, brokerages, developers and construction contractors who want leads, projects, money and reports in one system instead of separate spreadsheets.
Can I try Agentify ERP before paying?
Yes. New companies can start a free trial (7 days) with their own data at agentifyerp.co.
Is Agentify ERP only for Pakistan?
No. It is used from anywhere, and regional packs exist for Pakistan, the US, the UK, the UAE and Canada.
body: Agentify ERP is a cloud CRM and ERP for real estate agencies and construction companies. It runs in your browser, has an Android app, and keeps the work of a property or construction business in one workspace: who the customer is, what was sold or built, what was paid, and what is still due.
# Who it is for

It is made for property dealers and brokerages, developers selling on installments, and contractors who run projects with budgets and subcontractors. If your office currently runs on spreadsheets, a WhatsApp group and a separate accounting file, that is the situation Agentify ERP is meant to replace.
# Two products, so you only use what you need
Agentify ERP has two products, each with its own plans. You choose the one that matches your business.
* Real Estate: leads and follow-ups, property and project inventory, sales, installment plans with receipts, agent commissions, accounting, a customer portal and a website for your agency.
* Construction: projects and sites, bills of quantities (BOQ) and budgets, purchasing, materials, labour and subcontractors, client progress billing and a project schedule.
# One set of records

The idea behind the system is that a record is typed once. A sale builds its installment schedule, a receipt is applied to the right installment, and sales, receipts, expenses, vendor payments, commissions and salaries post to one double-entry accounting ledger. Reports then come from the same records your team works in, so the owner is not waiting for someone to reconcile three files.
# People and permissions

Access is controlled by roles. For example, a sales agent sees only their own leads and sales, while an accountant sees the money screens. Every change is logged, which helps when two people remember a payment differently.
# Help built in

Agentify ERP includes an assistant called Ask that answers how-to questions and questions about your data, including in Roman Urdu, and an AI writer that drafts property descriptions. You review what it writes before using it.
# How to evaluate it honestly

No software fits every office. Try it for a week with real leads and real receipts, not demo data, and check three things: can your agents use it on a phone without training, does it match the way you sell or bill, and can you get your data out if you leave. If you only keep a small contact list, a spreadsheet may be enough for now.
# Where to start
Most offices start with leads and receipts, then add installments, accounts and reports. You can start a free trial at agentifyerp.co, import a few real records, and decide from there.

title: Agentify ERP vs spreadsheets: what property dealers gain and give up
description: Honest comparison of Agentify ERP and spreadsheets for property dealers: leads, installments, receipts, commissions, and when Excel is enough.
faq: Is Agentify ERP better than Excel for property dealers?
For an office with several agents, installments and receipts, a connected system avoids retyping and mistakes. For one person with a short list, a spreadsheet can still be enough.
Can I import my Excel data into Agentify ERP?
Start by moving a few real records, such as current leads and open sales, so you can judge it with your own data during the free trial.
Do I have to stop using Excel completely?
No. Many offices keep spreadsheets for one-off analysis and use Agentify ERP as the single place for leads, sales and receipts.
body: Spreadsheets are where almost every property office starts, and they are good at it. They are free, familiar and flexible. The honest question is not whether spreadsheets are bad, but where they start to cost you money. This comparison looks at that for a property dealer, and at what Agentify ERP does differently.
# What spreadsheets do well
* Zero setup and zero cost for a small list.
* Anyone can change a column or add a formula.
* Good for one-off analysis, such as a quick commission estimate.
# Where spreadsheets start to hurt

The trouble begins when the same facts live in more than one file: the lead list, the sales sheet, the payment record and the commission sheet. Each needs retyping, and each can disagree with the others.
* A due date is edited and the history is lost.
* Two agents chase the same lead because nobody owns it.
* A receipt is written in one file and the balance is updated in another, sometimes days later.
* The owner cannot ask a quick question, such as how much is due this month, without someone building a report.
# What Agentify ERP does differently

Agentify ERP keeps these in one cloud workspace. A lead has an owner and a follow-up date. A sale builds its installment schedule. A receipt is applied to the right installment and updates the balance. Commissions follow rules the company sets, and sales, receipts and expenses post to one accounting ledger, so reports are built from the same records.
Roles control who sees what, so a sales agent sees only their own leads and sales, and every change is logged.
# What you give up

Honesty matters here. A spreadsheet will always be more flexible for odd, one-off layouts, and a system asks the team to follow a process. You also need an internet connection, although Agentify ERP has an Android app for the field.
# A practical way to decide
* One person and under a few dozen open files: a spreadsheet is probably fine.
* Several agents, installments, or an owner who wants live numbers: a connected system pays for itself in avoided mistakes.
* Not sure: start a free trial, move a few real leads and one installment sale, and compare the time it takes.
You can start a free trial of Agentify ERP at agentifyerp.co and keep your spreadsheets until you are comfortable.

title: Agentify ERP vs a generic CRM for real estate: what the ERP adds
description: Agentify ERP compared with a generic CRM for real estate: installments, receipts, commissions, inventory and accounts, and when a simple CRM is enough.
faq: What is the difference between a CRM and an ERP for real estate?
A CRM tracks leads and follow-ups. An ERP also covers inventory, sales, installments, receipts, commissions and accounts, so money and records stay connected.
Is Agentify ERP a CRM?
It includes a lead CRM, and it also covers properties, sales, installments, commissions and accounting for real estate.
When is a simple CRM enough?
If you only need to track enquiries and follow-ups and keep money records elsewhere, a simple CRM can be enough.
body: A generic sales CRM is a good tool for tracking people: who enquired, who was called, who is likely to buy. A property business also has to track things a generic CRM was not designed for: which plot or unit is sold, what the installment schedule is, what was paid, and what commission is owed. This article compares the two approaches fairly.
# What a generic CRM gives you
* A lead list with stages and reminders.
* Email and call logging.
* Reports on pipeline and activity.
If your main problem is that follow-ups are forgotten, this may be all you need, and a simple CRM is usually cheaper and quicker to roll out.
# What it usually leaves to other tools

Property sales add records that a generic CRM does not hold natively: inventory with status, installment plans, receipts that must match each installment, agent commissions and a ledger. Offices then bridge the gap with spreadsheets, and the gap is where mistakes live: a receipt that was never matched, a commission paid on the wrong amount.
# What Agentify ERP adds
Agentify ERP starts with the lead CRM and continues into the rest of the property workflow.
* Property and project inventory linked to sales.
* A sale that builds its installment schedule, with receipts applied to the right installment.
* Commissions that follow rules set by the company.
* Accounting where sales, receipts, expenses and vendor payments post to one double-entry ledger.
* A customer portal and a website for the agency.
# The trade-off

A fuller system asks more of you at the start: more fields, more roles and a process to follow. A simple CRM is lighter. The question is whether your cost is forgotten follow-ups or disconnected money records. Most offices that sell on installments find the second one larger.
# How to choose
* Track only enquiries: start with a simple CRM.
* Sell on installments, pay commissions or need accounts: look for a CRM that includes them.
* Run both real estate and construction: check that the same system covers both.
You can try Agentify ERP free at agentifyerp.co, with your own leads and one real sale, before deciding.

title: How a property dealer office can run its day on Agentify ERP
description: A walk through a property dealer office day on Agentify ERP: new leads, follow-ups, site visits, sales, installments, receipts and the owner view at night.
faq: Can agents use Agentify ERP on a phone?
Yes. It works in the mobile browser and there is an Android app.
Who sees my customers and sales?
Access is set by roles. For example, a sales agent sees only their own leads and sales.
Where do receipts go?
A receipt is applied to the right installment and updates the balance, and it posts to the accounts.
body: This is a walk through one ordinary day in a property dealer office using Agentify ERP, so you can picture the workflow before you try it. It describes how the product is meant to be used, not a customer story.
# Morning: new leads and follow-ups

Enquiries from portals, Facebook, WhatsApp and walk-ins are added to one lead list. Each lead has an owner and a next follow-up date, so the manager opens the list and sees what is due today and what is overdue instead of asking each agent.
# Midday: site visits and matching properties
Agents match a buyer to property or project inventory and record the visit. Because inventory sits next to the leads, nobody offers a plot that is already sold.
# Afternoon: closing a sale

When a buyer agrees, the sale is created. It builds the installment schedule, and the agent commission follows the company rule. The property status changes, so the website and the team see it as sold.
# Whenever money arrives: receipts
A receipt is recorded against the buyer and applied to the right installment, and the balance updates at once. It posts to the accounts, so the accountant does not retype it later.
# Evening: the owner view

The owner checks what was collected today, what is overdue, which agents are closing deals and which lead sources work. These numbers come from the same records the team used all day, so they do not need a separate report.
# Habits that make it work
* Add every enquiry the same day, with a follow-up date.
* Record a receipt the day the money arrives.
* Let each person use their own login, so changes are traceable.
# Try it with your own office
Start a free trial at agentifyerp.co and run one week of real leads and receipts through it. If the day above looks like yours, it is worth continuing.

title: How a contractor can control project costs with Agentify ERP
description: How a construction company can use Agentify ERP for BOQ, budgets, purchasing, labour, subcontractors and client billing to spot cost overruns early.
faq: Does Agentify ERP have a construction product?
Yes. It covers projects, sites, BOQs and budgets, purchasing, materials, labour, subcontractors, client billing and a project schedule.
Can I link purchases to the project budget?
Yes. Purchasing, site records and billing connect to the project, so spend is visible against the budget.
Do I need the real estate product too?
No. The Construction product has its own plans, and you choose the one your business needs.
body: Cost overruns rarely arrive in one piece. They creep in through materials bought above the estimate, extra labour days and variations nobody priced. This article shows how a contractor can use the Construction product of Agentify ERP to see the gap early, using the way the product is designed to work.
# Start from the BOQ and the budget

The bill of quantities lists each work item with a quantity, unit and rate. In Agentify ERP the BOQ and the project budget live with the project, so they become the baseline you compare everything against.
# Charge purchases to the project
Purchase requests and orders are raised against the project, and supplier bills are charged to it. When a purchase is made, you can see how much of that budget line is already spent.
# Record site work as it happens
Materials issued, labour and subcontractor work are recorded against the project, so cost does not appear for the first time in the monthly accounts.
# Bill the client from progress
Client progress billing follows completed work, and the project schedule shows planned against actual progress, which helps keep the invoice and the site in agreement.
# A weekly routine
* Compare budget with actual cost for each project every week.
* Approve purchases against a budget line.
* Price a variation the day it is agreed.
* Keep subcontractor measurements and payments in the same project record.
# Be realistic

No system replaces site discipline. If materials are not recorded when issued, the numbers will lag. The value of connecting these records is that gaps show up quickly, not that they disappear on their own.
# Try it on one project
Start a free trial at agentifyerp.co and set up one live project with its BOQ and budget. After a few weeks you will know whether the cost picture is clearer than in your spreadsheets.

title: How to choose real estate software: a checklist and where Agentify ERP fits
description: A vendor-neutral checklist for choosing real estate or construction software in Pakistan, with an honest note on where Agentify ERP fits and where not.
keyword: how to choose real estate software
faq: What should I check before buying real estate software?
Whether it matches how you sell or bill, whether agents can use it on a phone, who owns your data and whether you can export it, and whether you can try it with real records first.
Where does Agentify ERP fit?
It suits property and construction firms that want leads, sales, installments, projects and accounts in one cloud system, with a free trial.
When might Agentify ERP not be the right choice?
If you only need a contact list or a single-purpose tool, a lighter product or a spreadsheet may fit better.
body: Choosing business software is easier with a checklist than with a sales pitch. This one works for any real estate or construction product, and it ends with an honest note on where Agentify ERP fits and where it may not.
# 1. Start from your costly problems

Write down where you lose money or time today: forgotten follow-ups, unmatched receipts, commission disputes, cost overruns, reports that take days. Software should be judged against those, not against a feature list.
# 2. Check that it matches your business
* Do you sell on installments? The system should build and track the schedule.
* Do you pay commissions? They should follow your rules.
* Do you run projects with budgets and subcontractors? Look for BOQ and cost control.
* Do you need your own country, currency and tax rules?
# 3. Check it works for your people
Agents spend the day in the field. Make sure the system works on a phone without training, and that roles limit what each person can see.
# 4. Check data ownership and exit
Ask who owns your data, whether you can export it at any time, and what happens to it if you leave.
# 5. Try it with real records
A demo hides problems. Move a few real leads and one real sale into a free trial and see how it feels after a week.
# 6. Count the whole cost
Look at the plan price, the number of users, extras you will need, and the time your team spends learning it.
# Where Agentify ERP fits

Agentify ERP is a cloud CRM and ERP with a Real Estate product (leads, inventory, sales, installments, receipts, commissions, accounting, customer portal) and a Construction product (projects, BOQ, budgets, purchasing, labour, subcontractors, client billing). It fits firms that want these in one system, and it offers a free trial so you can test it with your own data.
# Where it may not fit

If you only need a contact list, or a single-purpose tool such as a basic lead tracker, a lighter product or a spreadsheet may be a better fit. Choose the smallest tool that solves your costly problems, and move up when the business needs it.
